content.rendered:
Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes. The believer is not asked to build the armor. The armor has been forged in heaven. The instruction is simply to put it on and stand.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, July 22, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Finally, be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes. For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms.”
Ephesians 6:10-12 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Paul closes Ephesians with one of the most quoted passages in the New Testament on spiritual warfare. Chained to a Roman soldier as he dictated the letter, Paul may well have been looking directly at the armor of his guard as he wrote. He picks up piece by piece the equipment of a Roman legionnaire and transforms each item into a spiritual reality already available to every believer in Christ.

The belt of truth. The breastplate of righteousness. The shoes of the readiness of the gospel of peace. The shield of faith. The helmet of salvation. The sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God. Six pieces, each corresponding to a specific defence against the enemy’s tactics. Paul then adds the seventh dimension that ties them all together. Praying in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests.

The critical detail most believers overlook is that Paul does not tell the Ephesians to fabricate the armor. Every piece already exists. The truth is already true. The righteousness is already imputed. The gospel of peace has already been proclaimed. The faith has already been given. The salvation has already been secured. The Word has already been spoken. The Spirit has already been sent. The armor is not manufactured on the fly by the believer under attack. It is put on. It has already been made. The believer is simply asked to walk into it and stand.

Paul’s language is worth reading carefully. Take your stand. Stand firm. Stand your ground. He uses the verb histēmi four times in this passage, and every time it is imperative. The believer’s posture is defensive, not aggressive. The believer is not being told to charge the enemy. The believer is being told to hold the ground Christ has already secured, in the armor Christ has already forged, in the day of evil that will come to every generation. The victory is not achieved by the believer running at the enemy. The victory is achieved by the believer standing firm in what Christ has provided.

For Gospelbuzz readers, the truth this morning is practical. Every piece of armor Paul names is already yours in Christ. The truth is yours in Christ. The righteousness is yours in Christ. The peace is yours in Christ. The faith is yours in Christ. The salvation is yours in Christ. The Word is yours in Christ. The Spirit is yours in Christ. Your task today is not to acquire the armor. Your task is to put it on. Consciously. Deliberately. Before the day begins. Then stand in it. The devil’s schemes will meet a fully-armoured believer who is not moving. And the devil’s schemes will fail.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that You have provided the full armor for every day I walk into. I put on the belt of truth. I put on the breastplate of righteousness. I put on the shoes of the readiness of the gospel of peace. I take up the shield of faith to extinguish every flaming arrow of the enemy. I put on the helmet of salvation. I take up the sword of the Spirit, Your Word. I pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers. I stand today, fully armoured in Christ, on the ground Jesus has already secured. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am clothed in the full armor of God. Every piece is mine in Christ. I stand today on the ground Jesus has already secured. The devil’s schemes fail against a fully-armoured believer.
